A comprehensive summary for our work would be that

the prevalence of silent MI is about 16% in patients with newly diagnosed diabetes, that it is independently associated with increased risk of fatal myocardial infarct and all-cause death, and that it adds little to current risk prediction models.
the presence of silent myocardial ischemia (SMI) was associated with a significantly increased risk of fatal and nonfatal myocardial infarctions (MIs).
silent myocardial infraction is associated with increased risk of future myocardial infraction and death, and that this association is independent of other risk factors for cardiovascular disease.
The main takeaway from our work is that
silent myocardial infraction, or silent heart attack, is associated with increased risk of fatal heart attacks, but it does not add to risk prediction beyond what is already known.
the presence of SMI is associated with a higher risk of future fatal myocardial infarctions and all-cause death in patients with type 2 diabetes.
the presence of SMI in newly diagnosed type 1 and type 2 diabetes is associated with a higher risk for future cardiovascular disease.
